{{nihongo|'''Niukawakami Shrine Kamisha'''|丹生川上神社上社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Yamato Province]].

'''Niukawakami Shrine Upper Shrine''' (にうかわかみじんじゃかみしゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in Sako, Kawakami Village, Yoshino District, Nara Prefecture. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myōjin Taisha|fr|Myōjin Taisha|ja|名神大社|simple|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|qid=Q9610964}}) and a {{ill|Shikinai Ronsha|ja|論社|qid=Q135022904}} of the {{ill|Twenty-Two Shrines|Q215320|qid=Q215320}} (lower 8). Its former {{ill|Q712534|lt=shrine rank}} was {{ill|Q712534|lt=Kanpei-taisha}}{{Efn2|However, that ranking was as a combined unit with the present Niukawakami Lower Shrine, or with all three including present Niukawakami Shrine (Middle Shrine).}}. Today it is a {{ill|Beppyo shrine|Q10898274|qid=Q10898274}} of {{ill|Association of Shinto Shrines|Q908077|qid=Q908077}}.

The name distinguishes it from {{ill|Niukawakami Lower Shrine|ja|丹生川上神社下社|zh|丹生川上神社下社|qid=Q10877367}} in {{ill|Shimoichi, Nara|Q1203064|qid=Q1203064}}.

يىلى|uk|1922|ur|1922ء|uz|1922|vec|1922|vi|1922|vls|1922|vo|1922|wa|1922|war|1922|wuu|1922年|xmf|1922|yi|1922|za|1922 nienz|zea|1922|zh|1922年|zh_classical|一九二二年|zh_min_nan|1922 nî|zh_yue|1922年|qid=Q2165}} (Taishō 11) with present {{ill|Niukawakami Shrine (Q246370)|abstract|Q246370|fr|Niukawakami-jinja|ja|丹生川上神社|ru|Ниукаваками-дзиндзя|zh|丹生川上神社|qid=Q246370|lt=Niukawakami Shrine (Middle Shrine)}}, it was changed to Takaokami-no-Kami. Takaokami-no-Kami has long been regarded as a deity of rain and rain-stopping.

=== History ===
Until early {{ill|Meiji era|Q3125096|qid=Q3125096}}, it was a small shrine called Takaokami Shrine, with unclear origin. Excavation with construction of {{ill|Ohtaki Dam|ja|大滝ダム|ta|ஒக்டாகி அணை|uz|Ohtaki toʻgʻoni|qid=Q11437563}} discovered the Miyanotaira site{{Efn2|Early and late Jōmon pottery was found. Most stone tools were sinkers used in fishing nets, about 400 items.}}; directly under former main sanctuary remains were ritual-altar stones dating back before late Heian (late 11th century). Nearby were also found circular stone-arrangement remains with standing stones, seen as ritual remains from end of middle to early late {{ill|Jōmon period|ar|فترة جومون|az|Comon dövrü|ba|Дзёмон дәүере|bcl|Jōmon jidai|be|Дзёмон|bg|Джомон|bn|জোমোন যুগ|br|Marevezh Jōmon|ca|Període Jōmon|cs|Období Džómon|de|Jōmon-Zeit|eo|Ĵomon-epoko|es|Período Jōmon|et|Jōmoni ajastu|eu|Jōmon aroa|fa|دوره جومون|fi|Jōmon-kausi|fo|Jomontíðin|fr|Période Jōmon|he|תקופת ג'ומון|hi|जोमौन काल|hr|Razdoblje Jōmon|hu|Dzsómon-kor|id|Zaman Jomon|is|Jómontímabilið|it|Periodo Jōmon|ja|縄文時代|jv|Jaman Jomon|ka|ჯიომონის ეპოქა|ko|조몬 시대|lfn|Periodo Jomon|lt|Džiomon laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Jōmon|nl|Jomonperiode|no|Jōmon-kulturen|pl|Jōmon|pt|Período Jomon|ro|Perioada Jōmon|ru|Период Дзёмон|sh|Jomon|simple|Jōmon period|sk|Obdobie Džómon|sl|Obdobje Džomon|sr|Џомон период|sv|Jōmon|th|ยุคโจมง|tl|Panahong Jōmon|tok|tenpo Somon pi ma Nijon|tr|Jomon Dönemi|uk|Період Дзьомон|ur|جومون دور|vi|Thời kỳ Jōmon|war|Panahon Jōmon|wuu|绳纹时代|zh|繩紋時代|zh_classical|繩文時代|zh_min_nan|Zyômon sî-tāi|zh_yue|繩紋時代|qid=Q52824}} (about 4,000 years ago). Though a break is recognized through Nara and Kofun periods, shrine ritual space may trace back to Jōmon.

In {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} it was ranked {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Gōsha}}. But Etō Masazumi, assistant priest of then-Kanpei-taisha {{ill|Niukawakami Lower Shrine|ja|丹生川上神社下社|zh|丹生川上神社下社|qid=Q10877367|lt=Niukawakami Shrine}} (present lower shrine), argued lower shrine location did not match the four-boundary area in the 895 Daijōkan decree ('{{ill|Ruijū Sandai Kyaku|Q11665185|qid=Q11665185}}'), identifying this shrine as the Engishiki Niukawakami Shrine. In 1874 this shrine became under lower shrine jurisdiction; lower shrine called “Kuchi-no-miya” and this shrine “Oku-no-miya.” After Etō’s view was accepted, in {{ill|1896|Q7846|qid=Q7846}} “Kuchi-no-miya” was renamed “Niukawakami Lower Shrine,” this shrine “Upper Shrine,” and both together became “Kanpei-taisha Niukawakami Shrine.”

However, in {{ill|1915|Q2084|qid=Q2084}} (Taishō 4), Moriguchi Narakichi of Higashiyoshino (site of present middle shrine) published 'Study of Niukawakami Shrine,' arguing “Aritōri Shrine (present middle shrine) = Niukawakami.” This was accepted, and by Interior Ministry notice of Oct. 12, 1922, middle shrine was designated; upper and lower shrines were incorporated into it, and all three again treated together as “Kanpei-taisha Niukawakami Shrine.” At that time, upper shrine deity changed back from Mizuhanome-no-Kami to Takaokami-no-Kami, as in its Gōsha period.

=== Precincts ===
Current main sanctuary is three-bay nagare-zukuri with copper roof.
